property_summary: C.setSlopes reverts exactly when the slope kink is zero or >= 1e27, and succeeds for any kink in (0, 1e27).
For any valid kink, after setting zero slopes and limits, C.rate always returns an interest rate of 0 regardless of the vault's reported utilization.

On a freshly deployed C (initializers disabled by its constructor, access control unset), the access-guarded setters setSlopes and setLimits always revert, and rate returns 0 using default zero slopes as long as utilization is nonzero.
On a fresh C, setLimits always reverts and rate() returns exactly 0 regardless of parameters.
On a fresh C with unset access control, setLimits always reverts, and rate() returns 0 regardless of the vault's reported utilization.
On a fresh C, initialize(addr) succeeds exactly once; any subsequent initialize call reverts regardless of parameters.
setSlopes always reverts with InvalidKink whenever the kink is zero or >= 1e27, regardless of other parameters.
On a contract C that is not behind an ERC-1967 proxy (e.g. deployed directly and freshly initialized or not), upgradeToAndCall must always revert, for any implementation address and calldata.
On a freshly deployed, uninitialized C, any state-changing call (e.g. setSlopes with valid slopes) always reverts because the access check against the unset accessControl address cannot succeed.
C has no payable entry point: any call to it carrying nonzero Ether reverts and leaves address(c).balance unchanged at zero.
